## Equations Derivation

**NOTE: Baran and Wu use the DistFlow equations for a balanced, single-phase equivalent radial distribution system. We use these equations as a starting point for our unbalanced three-phase work.**

Consider the following single line diagram:

::: {#fig-SLD layout-ncol="1"}
![ht](/figures_qmd/Barans_paper_sld.png){width="80%"}

A single Line Diagram (SLD) for an $n$ bus system. The loads are unknown for now. The complex power ($\bar{S}$) flowing between each bus is shown.
:::

**For each load, we consider** $P_{L,n}$ and $Q_{L,n}$, indicating real and reactive power consumed at bus $n$. Positive load means consumption.

Each line has an impedance, $\bar{Z}_{n} = r_{n}+jx_{n}$. The sending-end complex power flow on each line is given by:

$$\bar{S}_{n} = P_{n}+jQ_{n}$$

For instance, for the line leaving bus $i+1$:

$$\bar{S}_{i+1} = P_{i+1}+jQ_{i+1}$$

## Deriving the Real and Reactive Power Equations

I think it is easier to see this if we look at the power flow between two consecutive buses. Consider the power flow between buses $n$ and $n+1$. We define $P_n$ as the power leaving bus $n$ and entering line $(n,n+1)$:

$$\underbrace{P_{n}}_{\text{Power leaving bus $n$}} = \underbrace{P_{n,loss}}_{\text{Line loss}} + \underbrace{P_{n+1}}_{\text{Power leaving bus $n+1$}} + \underbrace{P_{L,n+1}}_{\text{Load at bus $n+1$}}$$ {#eq-KCL}

### Decomposing the Losses term in equation @eq-KCL

$$P_{loss} = r |I|^{2}$$

At any given bus $n$:

$$P_{n,loss} = r_{n} |I_{n}|^{2}$$ {#eq-power_losses}

Recall:

$$\bar{S} = \bar{V}\bar{I}^{*} = P+jQ$$

Wherein the magnitude of the apparent power is given by:

$$|S| = |I|~|V| = \sqrt{P^{2} + Q^{2}}$$

Squaring both sides:

$$|S|^{2} = |I|^{2}~|V|^{2} = P^{2}+Q^{2}$$

Solving for the squared current magnitude:

$$|I|^{2} = \frac{P^{2} + Q^{2}}{|V|^{2}}$$

For the line leaving bus $n$, the squared current magnitude is:

$$|I_{n}|^{2} = \frac{P^{2}_{n} + Q^{2}_{n}}{|V_{n}|^{2}}$$ {#eq-current}

substituting the current equation @eq-current into @eq-power_losses we get:

$$P_{n,loss} = r_{n} \frac{P^{2}_{n} + Q^{2}_{n}}{|\bar{V}_{n}|^{2}}$$ {#eq-full-Plosses}

Substituting @eq-full-Plosses in the power balance between buses $n$ and $n+1$ in @eq-KCL, we get:

$$\underbrace{P_{n}}_{\text{Power leaving bus $n$}} = \underbrace{r_{n} \frac{P^{2}_{n} + Q^{2}_{n}}{|\bar{V}_{n}|^{2}}}_{\text{Line loss}} + \underbrace{P_{n+1}}_{\text{Power leaving bus $n+1$}} +\underbrace{P_{L,n+1}}_{\text{Load at bus $n+1$}}$$ {#eq-DistFlow-Real-Power-Equation}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Note

@eq-DistFlow-Real-Power-Equation is the real power DistFlow Equation. This is the exact branch real-power balance for the single-phase equivalent line model, assuming the bus has one downstream line and no additional injection. For a branching feeder, we also account for every outgoing branch.
:::

Similarly, the reactive power can be calculated in a similar manner:

$$\underbrace{Q_{n}}_{\text{Q leaving bus $n$}} = \underbrace{x_{n} \frac{P^{2}_{n} + Q^{2}_{n}}{|\bar{V}_{n}|^{2}}}_{\text{Reactive power absorbed in the line}} + \underbrace{Q_{n+1}}_{\text{Q leaving bus $n+1$}} +\underbrace{Q_{L,n+1}}_{\text{Q consumed by bus $n+1$ load}}$$ {#eq-DistFlow-Reactive-Power-Equation}

## Deriving the Voltage Equation:

Applying KVL to buses, $i$ and $i-1$ in @fig-SLD:

$$\bar{V}_{i-1} = \bar{Z}_{i-1}~\bar{I}_{i-1} + \bar{V}_{i}$$ {#eq-KVL}

The current complex value can be solved for in a similar manner as in equation @eq-current:

$$\bar{V}_{n}~\bar{I}_{n}^{*} = P_{n}+jQ_{n}$$

Taking the complex conjugate and solving for $\bar{I}_{n}$:

$$\bar{I}_{n} = \frac{P_{n}-jQ_{n}}{\bar{V}_{n}^{*}}$$ {#eq-complex-current}

Substituting @eq-complex-current in @eq-KVL & solving for $\bar{V}_{i}$:

$$\bar{V}_{i} = \bar{V}_{i-1} - \bar{Z}_{i-1}~\bar{I}_{i-1}$$ {#eq-KVL2}

$$\bar{V}_{i} = \bar{V}_{i-1} - \bar{Z}_{i-1}~\frac{P_{i-1}-jQ_{i-1}}{\bar{V}_{i-1}^{*}}$$

We can then extend this to get only the magnitude of the voltage:

Recall $|a-b|^{2} = (a-b)(a^{*}-b^{*})$:

$$|\bar{V}_{i}|^{2} = (\bar{V}_{i-1} - \bar{Z}_{i-1}~\bar{I}_{i-1})~(\bar{V}^{*}_{i-1} - \bar{Z}^{*}_{i-1}~\bar{I}^{*}_{i-1})$$

Multiplying both terms, we end up with:

$$|\bar{V}_{i}|^{2} = |\bar{V}_{i-1}|^{2} - 2~\Re \{\underbrace{\bar{V}^{*}_{i-1}~\bar{I}_{i-1}}_{\substack{\text{Apparent} \\ \text {Power} \\ \text{Conjugate}}}~\bar{Z}_{i-1}\} + |\bar{Z}_{i-1}|^{2}~|\bar{I}_{i-1}|^{2}$$ {#eq-voltage-ref1}

Recall $\bar{S}^{*}_{i-1} = \bar{V}^{*}_{i-1}~\bar{I}_{i-1} = P_{i-1} - jQ_{i-1}$

So the middle term can be decomposed such that:

$$\bar{V}^{*}_{i-1}~\bar{I}_{i-1}~\bar{Z}_{i-1} = (P_{i-1} - jQ_{i-1})(r_{i-1}+jx_{i-1})$$

Multiplying and obtaining only the real part because we are trying to calculate the magnitude:

$$\Re \{\bar{Z}_{i-1}~\bar{V}^{*}_{i-1}~\bar{I}_{i-1}\} = r_{i-1}~P_{i-1} + x_{i-1}~Q_{i-1}$$ {#eq-voltage-ref2}

The last term in @eq-voltage-ref1 can be simplified further. Recall that $|\bar{Z}_{i-1}|^{2} = r^{2}_{i-1} + x^{2}_{i-1}$ and $|\bar{I}_{i-1}|^{2} = \frac{P^{2}_{i-1}+Q^{2}_{i-1}}{|\bar{V}_{i-1}|^{2}}$

$$|\bar{Z}_{i-1}|^{2}~|\bar{I}_{i-1}|^{2} = (r^{2}_{i-1} + x^{2}_{i-1})~(\frac{P^{2}_{i-1}+Q^{2}_{i-1}}{|\bar{V}_{i-1}|^{2}})$$ {#eq-voltage-ref3}

Substituting @eq-voltage-ref2 and @eq-voltage-ref3 in @eq-voltage-ref1:

$$|\bar{V}_{i}|^{2} = |\bar{V}_{i-1}|^{2} - 2(r_{i-1}~P_{i-1} + x_{i-1}~Q_{i-1})+(r^{2}_{i-1} + x^{2}_{i-1})~\frac{P^{2}_{i-1}+Q^{2}_{i-1}}{|\bar{V}_{i-1}|^{2}}$${#eq-voltage-distflow}

Note that @eq-voltage-distflow is essentially:
$$|\bar{V}_{i}|^{2} = |\bar{V}_{i-1}|^{2} - 2(r_{i-1}~P_{i-1} + x_{i-1}~Q_{i-1})+\underbrace{(r^{2}_{i-1} + x^{2}_{i-1})}_{\text{Imedance }Z^{2}}\underbrace{~\frac{P^{2}_{i-1}+Q^{2}_{i-1}}{|\bar{V}_{i-1}|^{2}}}_{\text{Current }I^{2}}$$

$V = ZI$, making the last term a loss term. This loss term is a second order contribution associated with line losses. Assuming the losses insignificant, we can drop this term and the equation becomes:

$$|\bar{V}_{i}|^{2} = |\bar{V}_{i-1}|^{2} - 2(r_{i-1}~P_{i-1} + x_{i-1}~Q_{i-1})$$

Rearranging the equation:

$$(|\bar{V}_{i}|^{2} - |\bar{V}_{i-1}|^{2}) \approx 2(r_{i-1}~P_{i-1} + x_{i-1}~Q_{i-1})$$

Recall $a^{2} - b^{2} = (a-b)(a+b)$:

$$(|\bar{V}_{i}| - |\bar{V}_{i-1}|)(|\bar{V}_{i}| + |\bar{V}_{i-1}|) \approx 2(r_{i-1}~P_{i-1} + x_{i-1}~Q_{i-1})$$

Defining the voltage drop as: $\Delta V = |\bar{V}_{i-1}| - |\bar{V}_{i}|$:

$$\Delta V(|\bar{V}_{i}| + |\bar{V}_{i-1}|) \approx 2(r_{i-1}~P_{i-1} + x_{i-1}~Q_{i-1})$$

Solving for $\Delta V$:

$$\Delta V \approx \frac{2(r_{i-1}~P_{i-1} + x_{i-1}~Q_{i-1})}{(|\bar{V}_{i}| + |\bar{V}_{i-1}|)}$$

**Assuming the voltage difference between adjascent buses is small:**

$$|\bar{V}_{i}| \approx |\bar{V}_{i-1}| \approx V$$

Therefore,

$$|\bar{V}_{i}| + |\bar{V}_{i-1}| \approx 2V$$

substituting in the previous $\Delta V$ equation:

$$\Delta V \approx \frac{2(r_{i-1}~P_{i-1} + x_{i-1}~Q_{i-1})}{2V}$$

Cancelling the 2:

$$\Delta V \approx \frac{r_{i-1}~P_{i-1} + x_{i-1}~Q_{i-1}}{V}$${#eq-simplified-voltage-equation}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Note

@eq-voltage-distflow is the Voltage Magnitude DistFlow Equation. This equation applies exactly to each branch under the paper's single-phase equivalent series-impedance model. It does not, by itself, describe mutual coupling in an unbalanced three-phase system.
:::

## Three-phase Unbalanced System

Using the same KVL we used before, @eq-KVL2, we can set a system of equations for buses $i$ and $j$ such that $i$ is upstream of $j$:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}
\bar{V}^{a}_{j} \\
\bar{V}^{b}_{j} \\
\bar{V}^{c}_{j}
\end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix}
\bar{V}^{a}_{i} \\
\bar{V}^{b}_{i} \\
\bar{V}^{c}_{i}
\end{bmatrix}
-
\begin{bmatrix}
\bar{Z}^{aa}_{ij} & \bar{Z}^{ab}_{ij} & \bar{Z}^{ac}_{ij}\\
\bar{Z}^{ba}_{ij} & \bar{Z}^{bb}_{ij} & \bar{Z}^{bc}_{ij}\\
\bar{Z}^{ca}_{ij} & \bar{Z}^{cb}_{ij} & \bar{Z}^{cc}_{ij}
\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}
\bar{I}^{a}_{ij} \\
\bar{I}^{b}_{ij} \\
\bar{I}^{c}_{ij}
\end{bmatrix}
$$ {#eq-kvl-matrix-form}

Note that the diagonal elements of $\bar{Z}_{ij}$ are self-impedances, and the off-diagonal elements are mutual impedances. This is a three-phase line model; a line with fewer phases uses the appropriate reduced impedance matrix. Neutral and transformer modeling must be handled consistently in the feeder model.

For any given phase, the voltage equation can be extracted from the above matrix form. For instance:

$$\bar{V}^{a}_{j} = \bar{V}^{a}_{i} - \bar{Z}^{aa}_{ij}\bar{I}^{a}_{ij} - \bar{Z}^{ab}_{ij}\bar{I}^{b}_{ij} - \bar{Z}^{ac}_{ij}\bar{I}^{c}_{ij}$$ {#eq-vv-eq-Unbalanced}

We can rewrite the current terms in @eq-vv-eq-Unbalanced using complex power for each phase. At the sending end of line $(i,j)$:

$$\bar{S}^{a}_{ij} = \bar{V}^{a}_{i}(\bar{I}^{a}_{ij})^{*} = P^{a}_{ij}+jQ^{a}_{ij}$$
$$\bar{S}^{b}_{ij} = \bar{V}^{b}_{i}(\bar{I}^{b}_{ij})^{*} = P^{b}_{ij}+jQ^{b}_{ij}$$
$$\bar{S}^{c}_{ij} = \bar{V}^{c}_{i}(\bar{I}^{c}_{ij})^{*} = P^{c}_{ij}+jQ^{c}_{ij}$$

As a vector format, we can express the three complex power equations as:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}
\bar{S}^{a}_{ij} \\
\bar{S}^{b}_{ij} \\
\bar{S}^{c}_{ij}
\end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix}
\bar{V}^{a}_{i}(\bar{I}^{a}_{ij})^{*} \\
\bar{V}^{b}_{i}(\bar{I}^{b}_{ij})^{*} \\
\bar{V}^{c}_{i}(\bar{I}^{c}_{ij})^{*}
\end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix}
P^{a}_{ij}+jQ^{a}_{ij} \\
P^{b}_{ij}+jQ^{b}_{ij} \\
P^{c}_{ij}+jQ^{c}_{ij}
\end{bmatrix}
$$ {#eq-three-phase-power-vector}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Note

@eq-three-phase-power-vector is a $3\times1$ vector of **per-phase complex powers**. It is not equal to a $3\times3$ matrix. The full branch-power matrix used by Gan and Low, including cross-phase products, is discussed in the background file. Mutual coupling is already present in @eq-kvl-matrix-form through the off-diagonal impedances.
:::

### Derive the current equations

Consider the complex power for phase $a$ between two buses:

$$\bar{S}_{ij}^{a} = \bar{V}_{i}^{a}(\bar{I}_{ij}^{a})^{*}$$

Take the complex conjugate of both sides:

$$\left(\bar{S}_{ij}^{a}\right)^{*} = (\bar{V}_{i}^{a})^{*}\bar{I}_{ij}^{a}$$

Solving for $\bar{I}_{ij}^{a}$:

$$\bar{I}_{ij}^{a} = \frac{\left(\bar{S}_{ij}^{a}\right)^{*}}{(\bar{V}_{i}^{a})^{*}}$$

Which can be rewritten as:

$$\bar{I}_{ij}^{a} = \frac{P_{ij}^{a} - jQ_{ij}^{a}}{(\bar{V}_{i}^{a})^{*}}$$ {#eq-phase-a-current}

Solving for phases $b$ and $c$ using the same approach:

$$\bar{I}_{ij}^{b} = \frac{P_{ij}^{b} - jQ_{ij}^{b}}{(\bar{V}_{i}^{b})^{*}}$$ {#eq-phase-b-current}

$$\bar{I}_{ij}^{c} = \frac{P_{ij}^{c} - jQ_{ij}^{c}}{(\bar{V}_{i}^{c})^{*}}$$ {#eq-phase-c-current}

@eq-phase-a-current, @eq-phase-b-current, and @eq-phase-c-current can be used in our KVL equation @eq-kvl-matrix-form, such that:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}
\bar V_j^a \\
\bar V_j^b \\
\bar V_j^c
\end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix}
\bar V_i^a \\
\bar V_i^b \\
\bar V_i^c
\end{bmatrix}
-
\bar{Z}_{ij}
\begin{bmatrix}
\dfrac{P_{ij}^{a} - jQ_{ij}^{a}}{(\bar{V}_{i}^{a})^{*}} \\
\dfrac{P_{ij}^{b} - jQ_{ij}^{b}}{(\bar{V}_{i}^{b})^{*}} \\
\dfrac{P_{ij}^{c} - jQ_{ij}^{c}}{(\bar{V}_{i}^{c})^{*}}
\end{bmatrix}
$$ {#eq-KVL3}

@eq-KVL3 expresses the receiving-end voltage phasors as a function of the sending-end voltage phasors, branch impedance, and phase real and reactive power flows [@gan2014convex]:

$$\boxed{\mathbf{\bar V}_{j}=\mathbf f(\mathbf{\bar V}_{i},\mathbf{\bar Z}_{ij},\mathbf P_{ij},\mathbf Q_{ij})}$$

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Note

This is an **exact branch relationship**, not yet an explicit voltage-magnitude sensitivity to inverter reactive power injection. To connect an inverter at bus $k$ to voltages throughout the feeder, we must also use network current/power balance and the inverter injection convention. Gan and Low's squared-voltage matrix derivation is in the background file for reference.
:::
